mainTopic: Why children don't start new מקרא on שבת, why רב and רבי יוחנן explain the teacher's pay differently, and the reading traditions from סיני
overview: The משנה allows someone who may not benefit from another person to still have that person teach his sons and daughters מקרא. Earlier on the daf, רב said a מקרא teacher is paid for watching the children (שכר שימור), and רבי יוחנן said he is paid for teaching the trope (שכר פיסוק טעמים). The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא showing that pay for שבת is allowed when it is part of a longer hire. That knocks down the earlier reason why children don't start new material on שבת. The גמרא gives two new reasons instead: so fathers are free to enjoy שבת, or because children are too full from שבת meals to learn well. Next, the גמרא explains each side of the dispute. רבי יוחנן rejects 'watching' because girls don't need watching. רב rejects 'trope' because the trope is part of the Torah itself, which he learns from a פסוק in נחמיה. The amud ends with רבי יצחק's teaching that four reading traditions are a הלכה למשה מסיני, and the גמרא begins listing examples of each. The list of words written but not read continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The worker hired for שבת: payment and responsibility
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes. A worker paid by the day gets no pay for שבת and is not responsible for losses on שבת. A worker hired for a longer period is paid for שבת as part of the whole, so he is responsible.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the things he was watching got lost on שבת, he is not responsible for them. But if he was hired for a week, a month, a year, or seven years, he is paid for שבת too. So if things got lost on שבת, he is responsible.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ברייתא it began quoting just before this. The ברייתא shows that you may not get paid for שבת by itself, only as part of a longer job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A day worker gets no שבת pay, so on שבת he is only an unpaid watcher and is not responsible for losses. A worker hired for a week or longer has his שבת pay built into the whole job, so he may be paid for שבת and is a paid watcher even then. Since pay for שבת is fine when it is built into a longer hire, a problem with the teacher's שבת pay cannot be why children don't start new material on שבת. That is why the next step says 'אלא' and gives a new reason.

keyTerms.meaning: Responsibility to pay for a loss
Payment for שבת, which is forbidden if paid on its own
A worker hired for a week (here שבת means a week)
Here, a seven-year cycle

steps.confusionAlert: In this list, שבת means a week and שבוע means a seven-year period. It is the opposite of what you might expect.

phrases.english: If they were lost, he is not responsible for them.
phrases.notes: This is the day worker: he gets no pay for שבת, so that day he's like an unpaid watcher.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם הָיָה שְׂכִיר שַׁבָּת, שְׂכִיר חֹדֶשׁ,
phrases.english: But if he was hired for a week, hired for a month,
hired for a year, hired for seven years,
he gives him payment for שבת.
Therefore, if they were lost, he is responsible for them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a ברייתא that began before this section.
steps.raayaObject: That payment for שבת is forbidden unless it is part of a longer hire.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a worker hired to watch things.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier explanation that children don't start new material on שבת because the teacher may not take pay for שבת. The ברייתא shows that pay for שבת is allowed when it is built into a longer hire.

steps.title: New reason: so fathers are free for the מצוה of שבת
steps.stepSummary: Since the 'watching' reason fails, the גמרא gives a new reason. Children don't start a new section on שבת so their fathers stay free to enjoy שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is the reason children don't start a new section on שבת: so the children's fathers will be free for the מצוה of שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the earlier explanation and gives a fresh reason why children don't begin new material on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Teaching new material is hard and takes more of the father's time. That would cut into his עונג שבת. So the שבת rule has nothing to do with paying the teacher, and the problem from the ברייתא goes away.

keyTerms.meaning: Children do not start a new section on שבת
They will be free
The fathers of the children

phrases.english: Rather, with regard to שבת,
this is the reason they don't read for the first time:
so that the fathers of the children will be free
for the מצוה of שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the explanation that step 1 knocked down.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The שבת rule came from a problem with the teacher taking pay for שבת, which the ברייתא showed is allowed when built into a longer hire.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule exists to keep fathers free to enjoy שבת.

steps.title: Second reason: children are heavy from שבת eating
steps.stepSummary: A second option: on שבת children eat and drink more, so they feel sluggish and can't focus on new material. שמואל's teaching backs this up.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say: on שבת they eat and drink, and they feel heavy. As שמואל said: a change in routine is the start of stomach illness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second, different reason why children don't start new sections on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the reason is about the children themselves, not the fathers. Eating more than usual makes them sluggish, so they can't learn something new well. שמואל's rule shows that a change in eating habits affects the body.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say instead
They feel heavy and sluggish
A change in routine

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
because on שבת they eat and drink
and their world is heavy on them.
phrases.notes: They feel sluggish and can't concentrate.

phrases.english: As שמואל said:
A change in routine is the start of stomach illness.

steps.whatToRemember: The rule against starting new material on שבת is not about the teacher's pay. It is either to keep fathers free to enjoy שבת, or because children are too full to learn well.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second reason alongside step 2.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule is about the teacher's pay.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule is because the children are heavy from eating.

steps.title: Why doesn't רבי יוחנן say the pay is for watching?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the one who says the pay is for teaching trope did not say it was for watching.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says it is payment for teaching the trope, why didn't he say it is payment for watching?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now looks at the two opinions about the teacher's pay. It starts by asking about the trope opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Paying for watching is simple and allowed, so it would seem like an easy explanation. The גמרא wants to know why רבי יוחנן rejected it.

keyTerms.meaning: Teaching the trope and punctuation of the verses
Payment for watching the children
What is the reason?

phrases.english: And according to the one who says it is payment for the trope,
phrases.notes: This is רבי יוחנן's view from earlier on the daf.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר שְׂכַר שִׁימּוּר?
phrases.english: what is the reason he didn't say payment for watching?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר שְׂכַר פִּיסּוּק טְעָמִים מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the dispute about the teacher's pay.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי יוחנן did not accept שכר שימור.

steps.title: Girls don't need watching
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the משנה also talks about teaching daughters, and girls don't need watching. So the pay can't be for watching.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds: do girls need watching?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question in step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allows teaching both sons and daughters. Girls usually stayed home and did not need to be watched. Watching can't explain the pay for girls, so רבי יוחנן says it is for the trope.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds
Daughters

phrases.aramaic: קָסָבַר בָּנוֹת מִי קָא בָּעֲיָין שִׁימּוּר?
phrases.english: He holds: do girls need watching?
phrases.notes: This is a rhetorical question. The answer is no, and the משנה mentions daughters too.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָסָבַר בָּנוֹת מִי קָא בָּעֲיָין שִׁימּוּר
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Daughters don't need watching, so the pay must be for something else.

steps.title: Why doesn't רב say the pay is for the trope?
steps.stepSummary: Now the גמרא asks the opposite question: why didn't the one who says watching say trope?
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says it is payment for watching, why didn't he say it is payment for the trope?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the same question around and asks it about the second opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The trope explanation works for both boys and girls. So why would רב stay with watching, which seems not to fit girls?

phrases.english: And according to the one who says it is payment for watching,
phrases.notes: This is רב's view from earlier on the daf.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר שְׂכַר פִּיסּוּק טְעָמִים?
phrases.english: what is the reason he didn't say payment for the trope?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר שְׂכַר שִׁימּוּר מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רב did not accept שכר פיסוק טעמים.

steps.title: The trope is part of the Torah itself
steps.stepSummary: רב holds that the trope is דאורייתא, so it counts as Torah. Taking pay for it would be forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds that the trope is from the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 6 and finishes the comparison between the two opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You may not take money for teaching Torah. If the trope is part of the Torah itself, paying for it is forbidden too. So the only allowed pay left is for watching.

keyTerms.meaning: From the Torah itself

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן says the pay is for trope, because girls don't need watching. רב says the pay is for watching, because the trope is Torah and can't be paid for.

phrases.english: He holds that the trope
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets.

phrases.english: is from the Torah.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The trope is Torah, so paying for it is forbidden.

steps.title: רב reads a פסוק in נחמיה as including the trope
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves that רב holds the trope is דאורייתא. He explains a פסוק in נחמיה as listing the Torah text, its translation, verse divisions, and the trope.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is as רב איקא בר אבין said in the name of רב חננאל in the name of רב: What does the פסוק mean, 'And they read in the book, in the Torah of God, distinctly, and they gave the sense, and caused them to understand the reading'? 'They read in the book, in the Torah of God' is the text itself. 'Distinctly' is the Aramaic translation. 'They gave the sense' is the verse divisions. 'Caused them to understand the reading' is the trope. Some say this last part means the מסורות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up step 7. It shows a teaching of רב where the trope comes from a פסוק, so for him the trope counts as Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 7 the גמרא claimed that רב holds the trope is דאורייתא. Here is the proof: רב reads the last phrase of the פסוק, 'caused them to understand the reading', as the trope. Since the trope is part of the Torah reading described in the פסוק, a teacher may not take pay for teaching it.

keyTerms.meaning: Distinctly, clearly. רב explains it as the Aramaic translation.
The Aramaic translation of the Torah
Here it means the division of the text into verses
Marking the text with trope (cantillation notes)
The traditions about how words are spelled and read

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why, according to רב, the teacher's pay cannot be for teaching trope. It must be for watching the children.

phrases.english: As Rav Ika bar Avin said
that Rav Chananel said that Rav said:
What is the meaning of what is written:
"And they read in the book, in the Torah of God, distinctly;
and they gave the sense, and caused them to understand the reading"?
"They read in the book, in the Torah of God": this is the text itself.
"Distinctly": this is the Aramaic translation.
"And they gave the sense": these are the verse divisions.
"And caused them to understand the reading": this is the trope.
And some say: these are the traditions of spelling and reading.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב אִיקָא בַּר אָבִין אָמַר רַב חֲנַנְאֵל אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for step 7's claim that רב holds the trope is דאורייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That רב holds the trope is part of Torah (דאורייתא)
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's reading of נחמיה 8:8, where 'ויבינו במקרא' means the trope
steps.whatToRemember: For רב, the trope is part of Torah, learned from the פסוק in נחמיה. So teaching it is teaching Torah, and a teacher may not take pay for it.

steps.title: רבי יצחק: reading traditions go back to סיני
steps.stepSummary: On a related note, רבי יצחק teaches that four reading and writing traditions are a הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: the vowel readings of the scribes, the ornamentation of the scribes, words read but not written, and words written but not read are all a הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a related teaching about how the Torah text is read. It lists four traditions that all come from משה at סיני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This connects to the topic of trope and מסורות: details of how we read the Torah are not later inventions. רבי יצחק names four kinds, and the גמרא will now explain them one by one.

keyTerms.meaning: The vowel readings of the scribes
The ornamentation of the scribes
Words that are read aloud but not written in the text
Words that are written in the text but not read aloud
A law handed down orally to משה at סיני

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
The vowel readings of the scribes, and the ornamentation of the scribes,
and words that are read but not written,
and words that are written but not read,
are a law given to Moses at Sinai.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A related teaching about reading traditions, following the mention of trope and מסורות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מקרא סופרים, עיטור סופרים, קרי ולא כתיב, and כתיב ולא קרי are all הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.confusionAlert: Even though the name says 'סופרים' (scribes), רבי יצחק is saying these traditions are not something the scribes made up. They go back to משה at סיני.

steps.title: Examples of the scribes' vowel readings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives examples of מקרא סופרים: the words ארץ, שמים, and מצרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: מקרא סופרים: for example ארץ, שמים, מצרים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts explaining רבי יצחק's list. It gives examples of the first item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are common words whose vowels change in certain places in a פסוק, such as at a pause. The way we vowel them is a tradition, not something visible in the letters alone.

keyTerms.meaning: Land; at a pause the vowel changes (from אֶרֶץ to אָרֶץ)
Heaven; its vowels also change at a pause
Egypt; its vowels also change at a pause

phrases.english: The vowel readings of the scribes:
'aretz' (land), 'shamayim' (heaven), 'Mitzrayim' (Egypt).
phrases.notes: The letters stay the same, but at a pause in the פסוק the vowels change, like אֶרֶץ becoming אָרֶץ.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first item in רבי יצחק's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מקרא סופרים means the traditional vowel readings of words like ארץ, שמים, and מצרים.

steps.title: Examples of the scribes' ornamentation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives examples of עיטור סופרים: several פסוקים with the word אחר, and one from תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: עיטור סופרים: 'afterward you shall go on', 'afterward she will go', 'afterward you will be gathered', 'the singers go before, the minstrels after', 'Your righteousness is like the mighty mountains'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second item in רבי יצחק's list by giving examples from the פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are places where the wording is read in a specific, polished way that the tradition set down. The גמרא only lists the examples here and does not explain each one.

keyTerms.meaning: After, afterward. It appears in most of the examples.
Musicians, minstrels
Mighty mountains (literally, 'mountains of God')

phrases.english: The ornamentation of the scribes:
"Afterward you shall go on"; "afterward she will go";
"afterward you will be gathered";
"The singers go before, the minstrels after";
"Your righteousness is like the mighty mountains."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second item in רבי יצחק's list, after the examples of מקרא סופרים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עיטור סופרים covers set traditional wordings such as אחר תעברו, אחר תלך, אחר תאסף, קדמו שרים אחר נגנים, and צדקתך כהררי אל.

steps.title: Words that are read but not written
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא lists seven places in נביאים and כתובים where a word is said out loud during the reading even though it does not appear in the written text.
steps.simpleTranslation: Read but not written: 'Euphrates' in 'as he went'; 'man' in 'as if a man inquired of the word of God'; 'come' in 'shall be built'; 'her' in 'escape'; 'את' in 'it has been told me'; 'to me' in 'the threshing floor'; 'to me' in 'the barley'. These are read but not written.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives examples of the third tradition from רבי יצחק's list: words we say out loud when reading, even though they are missing from the written text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each example names the missing word, then names a nearby word in the פסוק so you can find the spot. The written text has no letters there, but the tradition from סיני tells the reader to add the word. The list ends by repeating its heading to show the list is finished.

keyTerms.meaning: Read but not written: a word said out loud that has no letters in the text
These (Aramaic)
The river Euphrates
Escape; survivors
Threshing floor

steps.confusionAlert: The second word in each pair (like בלכתו or הגרן) is not the missing word. It is only a marker telling you which פסוק and where in it the missing word belongs.

phrases.english: Words that are read but not written:
"Euphrates" of "as he went";
"Man" of "as if a man inquired of the word of God";
"Come" of "shall be built";
"Her" of "escape";
"את" of "it has been told me";
"To me" of "the threshing floor";
"To me" of "the barley";
These are read but not written.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of examples for רבי יצחק's traditions, moving from עיטור סופרים to words that are read but not written.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Seven words in נביאים and כתובים are read aloud even though they are not written in the text, based on a tradition from סיני.

steps.title: Words that are written but not read
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins the last category: words that appear in the written text but are skipped when reading aloud, starting with the word נא in the פסוק about forgiving.
steps.simpleTranslation: And written but not read: 'נא' of 'may God forgive'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens the fourth tradition from רבי יצחק's list, the opposite of the last one: words that are written but not said out loud. It gives the first example, and the list continues.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the letters are really in the text, but the reader skips them. The first example is the word נא in the פסוק where נעמן asks that he himself ('your servant') be forgiven. This is the mirror image of step 12, where a word was said but had no letters.

keyTerms.meaning: Written but not read: a word with letters in the text that is skipped when reading aloud
Please; may (a word of request)
He will forgive

steps.whatToRemember: Together, the two lists show that the way we read the תנ״ך aloud is not always exactly what is written, and both the added words and the skipped words are a tradition from סיני.

phrases.english: And words that are written but not read:
"נא" of "may He forgive";
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 5:18. The list continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from words that are read but not written to the opposite category, words that are written but not read.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Some words appear in the written text but are not read aloud, such as נא in the פסוק about forgiving, and this is a tradition from סיני.
